purpose: Verify the 600-series charter and current DEFERRED state are aligned with the Portfolio Stewardship Framework v1.0 (S725). Confirm no charter conflicts with active governance standards.
reference_documents: S725 Portfolio Stewardship Framework v1.0 (492 lines, Agent O)
S725 Post-700 Governance Model v1.0 (Agent B)
S725 Governance Detection Standard v1.0 (Agent B)
S725 Scan Methodology Standard v1.0 (Agent G)
S726 Series Closure Gate v1.0 (Agent B)

lane_definition.framework_reference: S725 Portfolio Stewardship Framework §Lane 600 — Content Operations
lane_definition.framework_status: DEFERRED — S724 Executive Board unanimous decision (26/26 agents)
lane_definition.detail: Both the Framework and the Charter define the 600-series as DEFERRED. The Framework (published at S725) post-dates the Charter (created at S600) by the same session group. No drift. Both documents cite S724 as the deferral authority.

primary_owner.framework_reference: S725 Row 16: 'Governance Board (collective)' — deferred lane stewardship
primary_owner.charter_reference: S600 Charter §9.4: 'Ownership: Governance Board (deferred stewardship per S725 Row 16)'
primary_owner.detail: Both documents assign primary stewardship to the Governance Board. The Framework explicitly marks acceptance as PENDING (GAP-3). The Charter is subordinate to the Framework per §9.3 — in any conflict, the Framework prevails. Alignment is design-level correct but acceptance-level incomplete.

scope_boundaries.framework_reference: S725 Lane 600 Boundary Rules: MAY (charter preservation, design reference), MAY NOT (consume sessions, produce deliverables, create artifacts, interact with active lanes)
scope_boundaries.charter_reference: S600 Charter §2.2 IS NOT prohibitions: analytics (300), governance (700), certification (800), scoring, calibration, portfolio prioritization
scope_boundaries.detail: The Framework's boundary rules are more restrictive than the Charter's operational specification — this is by design. The Framework defines the lane at the portfolio level (static definition). The Charter defines the lane at the operational level (what agents would do if activated). The Framework's tighter restrictions reflect the DEFERRED state — the Charter's broader scope reflects the design intent. No contradiction: one describes what IS (dormant), the other describes what WOULD BE (active).

activation_conditions.framework_reference: S725 Lane 600 Succession Plan: 'Reactivation requires: (1) all 5 criteria from S724 Agent V, (2) 800-series certification complete or binding constraint shifted, (3) new Executive Board vote, (4) full T0 governance baseline'
activation_conditions.charter_reference: S600 Charter §5: 4 mandatory activation conditions (Economic Gate, Board Approval, No Ownership Conflict, Pre-Launch Baseline)
activation_conditions.detail: Both documents require a new Executive Board vote and T0 baseline. The Framework adds S724 Agent V's 5 criteria as an additional layer. The Charter acknowledges S724 as the source of the deferral decision (§0). S602's Activation Trigger Registry harmonizes all sources. No conflict.

closure_gate_compatibility.framework_reference: S726 Series Closure Gate v1.0: applies to any 600-series activation and subsequent closure
closure_gate_compatibility.charter_reference: S600 Charter §7 Deactivation Protocol: 'Closure subject to the Series Closure Gate (S726)'
closure_gate_compatibility.detail: The Charter explicitly subjects itself to the S726 Closure Gate. The 4-step chain (TRANSFER → ACCEPTANCE → APPROVAL → CLOSE) applies to both activation (600-series state transition from DEFERRED to ACTIVE) and deactivation (from ACTIVE back to DEFERRED or CLOSED). This is forward-compatible with all governance standards.

principles.label: No Orphaned Responsibility
principles.detail: S725 Row 16 is assigned to Governance Board but not accepted (GAP-3, 0/6). Per P1, responsibility is effectively orphaned despite assignment. The Framework was designed to prevent this — the violation exists because the assignment happened at S725 but acceptance has not occurred through S726, S727, or S601.
principles.resolution: Governance Board must explicitly accept S725 Row 16. Not a 600-specific issue — affects all 6 GAPs.

principles.label: Ownership Transfers Require Acceptance
principles.detail: The ownership assignment from the post-S723 handoff to S725 Row 16 skipped ACCEPTANCE. Per P2, the original owner (post-S723 maintenance mode) retains ownership until S725 Row 16 is explicitly accepted.
principles.resolution: Same as P1. Governance Board acceptance closes this violation.

principles.label: Series Closure Requires Ownership Disposition
principles.detail: The 600-series is DEFERRED, not CLOSED. Ownership disposition (P3 trigger) has not fired. When the lane eventually closes (activation → execution → deactivation per §7), the disposition requirement applies.

principles.label: Reviewable at Every Boundary
principles.detail: The lane is reviewed at every session boundary touching it (S600 Charter creation, S601 Activation Review, S602 Dormancy Governance). The annual cadence (S725 Row 16) and bi-session stewardship review cadence satisfy P4.

principles.label: Single Point of Accountability
principles.detail: S725 Row 16 assigns 'Governance Board (collective)' — collective ownership violates P5's 'single point of accountability' standard. However, S601 Agent D flagged this as anomaly P5. The Framework was designed with collective ownership for deferred lanes because no single agent is responsible for a dormant lane. This is an accepted tension: P5 applies to active lanes; deferred lanes may use collective stewardship with annual review cadence to prevent indefinite dormancy.

stewardship_principles_compliance.overall_compliance: PARTIALLY COMPLIANT — P1/P2 violations are governance-process issues (GAP-3), not charter defects. P5 is an accepted tension for deferred lanes.

600_100.detail: S600 Charter does not define a 100-series boundary. The 600-series was designed as a content drafting lane, not a platform lane. 100-series maintains runtime (app.js, index_updated.html, styles.css) — no overlap with 600-domain content preparation.

600_300.detail: Boundary is consumption-only (600 reads 300 outputs, may not produce analytics). S601 Agent C noted registry stats report to 300 creates a cross-lane data flow. Accepted as LOW severity (C-004). S602 classifies as ACCEPTED.

600_700.detail: Governor/governed relationship. Charter §3.2 explicitly subordinates 600 to 700 governance standards. C-002 (template vs. standard boundary) carries forward. S725 Governance Detection Standard and Scan Methodology Standard apply to 600 operations if activated — no exemption.

600_800.detail: Decider/supporter relationship. Charter §3.3 explicitly prohibits 600 from certification decisions. C-001 (handoff friction) carries forward. S725 G-NEW-1 through G-NEW-5 certification-blocking rules apply to any 600-prepared material consumed by 800.

600_500.detail: 500-series is CLOSED. No active lane operations. Case-bank is Certified at 100%. No interaction path exists.

governance_guard_compatibility.rule_1: Would apply to 600 if activated — question_state changes trigger WARN at session idle
governance_guard_compatibility.rule_2: Would apply to 600 if activated — DL-008 detection BLOCKs pack-file writes
governance_guard_compatibility.rule_3: Would apply to 600 if activated — BLOCKs MASTER_QUESTION_REGISTRY.md hand-edits (C-003 tension acknowledged)
governance_guard_compatibility.rule_4: Would apply to 600 if activated — answer-key changes trigger WARN at session idle
governance_guard_compatibility.rule_5: Would apply to 600 if activated — BLOCKs writes touching >30 question objects
governance_guard_compatibility.guard_conflict: NONE in dormant state. If activated, all 5 rules mechanically BLOCK prohibited operations (Agent F Scenarios 1-3 confirm). The guard's self-protection gap (COND-S726-004) and batch-cap vulnerability (Agent F Scenario 3) are pre-existing governance issues — not 600-specific.

s601_anomaly_reassessment.description: S601 Agent D identified 4 anomalies in charter stewardship compatibility (67/100 score). S602 reassesses each.

anomalies.label: Collective ownership (Governance Board)
anomalies.s601_status: Violates P5 Single Point of Accountability
anomalies.s602_reassessment: ACCEPTED for DEFERRED state. For deferred lanes, 'collective stewardship with annual review cadence' is the intended pattern (S725 Row 16). P5 applies strictly to active lanes. During activation, a single primary owner must be designated.

anomalies.label: Skipped ACCEPTANCE in activation path
anomalies.s601_status: No acceptance gate at activation — Stewardship P2 violated
anomalies.s602_reassessment: RESOLVED by S726 Series Closure Gate. The 4-step chain (TRANSFER → ACCEPTANCE → APPROVAL → CLOSE) now applies to activation as a state transition. ACCEPTANCE is required per S726 §2.

anomalies.label: Inconsistent primary-owner references
anomalies.s601_status: S600 Charter says 'Governance Board'; S725 says 'Governance Board (collective)'; REVISION_HISTORY says 'Executive Board directive'
anomalies.s602_reassessment: RESOLVED. The governance hierarchy is: Executive Board (voted S724 DEFER) > Governance Board (stewardship of lane per S725 Row 16). The REVISION_HISTORY reference to 'Executive Board directive' is the charter's creation authority, not its steward. No inconsistency.

anomalies.label: Registry boundary ambiguity
anomalies.s601_status: S600 §4.1 Agent A maintains registry; AGENTS.md Rule 3 blocks hand-edits
anomalies.s602_reassessment: ACCEPTED as LOW (C-003). Resolution path defined. Not blocking for DEFERRED state.

s601_anomaly_reassessment.revised_rationale: Two of four anomalies resolved by S726 Closure Gate and clearer ownership hierarchy documentation. P5 and Registry anomalies downgraded to ACCEPTED for DEFERRED state. Score improved from 67 to 85 (adjusted for dormant-state applicability). Remaining deductions: -10 for P1/P2 violations (GAP-3 acceptance), -5 for C-001/C-002 CARRY_FORWARD (procedural, awaiting activation).

verdict: ALIGNED. The S600 Reserve Charter is structurally aligned with the Portfolio Stewardship Framework v1.0. All lane definitions, boundary rules, activation conditions, and closure gate compatibility checks pass. Two P1/P2 violations are governance-process issues (GAP-3 ownership acceptance) affecting all deferred gaps — not charter-specific defects. Four S601 anomalies are either resolved (ACCEPTANCE path, primary-owner references) or accepted for dormant-state governance (P5 collective ownership, registry tension). No charter amendment is required.
recommendation: No charter amendments required. Maintain current alignment. Resolve GAP-3 (Governance Board acceptance) in next governance session. Re-verify alignment at next stewardship review or if activation conditions change.
